FINDING 1 (D052 item 1 — token-source comparability). The two accountings apply the IDENTICAL formula — tokens_in = input + cache_read, tokens_out = output — but to DIFFERENT provider-reported usage objects (verified in tools/runner claude-envelope path and tools/token-capture.py parse_session). They are NOT cross-family comparable as they stand:
  - cache reads: Claude's envelope carries cache_read_input_tokens (large — the cached system prompt + tools); the pi session carries cacheRead — deepseek (cloud) reported cacheRead>0 in at least one lane (aspect-crash dspro: 33024), qwen (local ollama) reported cacheRead=0 in all four of its lanes. So the fresh/cache SPLIT is provider-dependent even inside the pi path.
  - system prompt: both count their harness's system prompt, but the harnesses differ (Claude Code CLI vs pi), so the baseline differs; Claude's is largely cache_read, pi's is re-sent as fresh input on every turn.
  - tool results: both count tool results as input (same treatment), but the amount depends on how much each agent tooled.
  - reasoning/thinking: NOT symmetric. Claude's output_tokens includes thinking tokens (output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens is a subset of the same total), so tokens_out counts thinking. The pi session reports reasoning as a SEPARATE key, and tokens_out = output EXCLUDES it (verified: aspect-crash deepseek reasoning=12483, output=12855, recorded tokens_out=12855).
  - no-cache re-send inflation: a no-cache model (qwen, and deepseek on cache-miss) re-sends the full context every turn and each turn's input counts it fully; a caching model reports the repeated part as cache_read. tokens_in (input+cache_read) therefore has ONE definition — 'total prompt tokens read' — but the fresh/cache split is provider-dependent, and a no-cache model's input is inflated relative to a caching model's input for the same logical work.
  BOTTOM LINE: the grand-race ledger carries only tokens_in/tokens_out (not the cache_read/cache_write/reasoning split), so a cross-family COST comparison is INVALID on the current aggregate. tokens_out is roughly comparable only for non-reasoning work; tokens_in is not comparable cross-family at all. A valid comparison needs the per-family usage breakdown (cache_read vs input, reasoning vs output) plus a price table (tokens-now-prices-later doctrine, docs/infra/bakeoff.md). The breakdown exists in the pi session JSONLs and the claude envelope tees but is not surfaced per-lane in the ledger.

FINDING 2 (D052 item 2 — aspect-crash self-identification). 5/5 aspect-crash lanes are flagged self_identified=true in round 2 (fable, dspro, sonnet, haiku + qwen from the warm re-run; D052 named four because the qwen lane had not yet run). Every self_id_match is a model label that appears in the packet's OWN fixture — resume-output.txt / STATE.md name kimi-k2.7, deepseek-v4-flash, glm-5.2 as prior claimants and next dispatches. NO lane matched its own canonical label (e.g. fable's answer says 'claim T529 --agent deepseek-v4-flash' and 'T528 stays with kimi-k2.7' — fixture-quoted OTHER models). So G4's label-matching self-identification flag is a FALSE POSITIVE for this packet: the answer-keyed output NECESSARILY repeats model names from the fixture, so the flag measures 'did the lane quote the fixture' (which a correct answer must), not 'did the lane reveal its own identity'. This is a property of the packet, not a lane behaviour. GRADING HAZARD: the sanitizer redacts those fixture-quoted labels (out.sanitized.md turns 'claim T529 --agent deepseek-v4-flash' into 'claim T529 --agent [SELF-IDENTIFICATION REDACTED]'), which can turn a CORRECT answer into an ungradeable one. The grader must NOT treat aspect-crash self_identified=true as a family leak, and must grade aspect-crash from out.md (or re-derive), not out.sanitized.md.
